case_name: Sabeeha Faikage and others v Union of India and others
facts: The husbands/sons of the petitioners were recruited and placed through respondent nos. 4 and 5 to work as Seafarers on tugboat Jupiter-6 carrying the flag of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines.
On 21.08.2005, Jupiter-6 along with its crew comprising 10 Indians and 3 Ukrainians, left Walvis Bay in Namibia and was towing a dead ship Satsung on its way to Alang in Gujarat in India.
On 05.09.2005, Jupiter-6 went missing in the high seas.
On 25.04.2006, however, the respondent no. 4 sent a letter to the petitioners saying that all efforts to search the missing Jupiter-6 and her 13 crew members have proved unproductive...

Finally, the petitioners received the communication dated 17.08.2006 from the Government of India, Ministry of Shipping, Government Shipping Office, Mumbai, certifying that their husbands/sons were presumed to be dead.
issues: The safety of Indian citizens on board of foreign flag vessels
In case such Indian citizens on board a foreign flag vessel lost their lives, the compensation payable to their kith and kin
petitioner_arguments: u/art. 32 of the Constitution complaining of the breach of the fundamental right to life u/art. 21 of the Constitution.

The petitioners have prayed for inter alia a writ of mandamus/direction to the respondents to conduct an investigation into the mysterious disappearance of their husbands/sons who were on board Jupiter6.
respondent_arguments: They became aware of the casualty for the first time when they received a communication dated 10.10.2005 about the incident from respondent no. 4 and that the administration of the State (India) was not invited to participate in the investigation as per para 4 of M.S. Notice 26 of 2002.
court_reasoning: We find that the counter affidavit filed by the Indian Government does not furnish necessary and sufficient details.

A reading of the para 4 of the order dated 24.09.2008 would show that this Court limited the scope of the writ petition to two issues: (i) the safety of Indian citizens on board of foreign flag vessels and (ii) in case such Indian citizens on board a foreign flag vessel lost their lives, the compensation payable to their kith and kin.
holding: The Court directed that a sum of 2,85,000 US Dollars for the remaining nine Indian seafarers be deposited in Court for payment to their family members without prejudice to their claims for higher compensation.

The Court permitted the legal heirs/representatives of the officers/seamen to lodge their claims for disbursement of compensation with the Registrar (Judicial) who was required to verify the claims and submit a report to this Court with regard to disbursement.
